memory_update.text: Add NOW, CRM, PLTR, MSFT, ORCL, SAP, WDAY, ADBE, PATH, SNOW, MDB, DDOG, CRWD, IBM, and TEAM to the enterprise AI automation/data workflow platform universe.
The strongest chokepoint signal is not model access; it is control of trusted enterprise context, permissions, workflow execution, auditability, and outcome measurement inside systems of record.

Confluent should not be tracked as an independent US-listed ticker in this layer if IBM acquisition completion is confirmed in the dashboard security master; map streaming-data exposure to IBM unless a separate listed instrument remains.

Private vendors such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Writer, Glean, Moveworks, n8n, and many vertical-agent startups are important competitive/customer evidence but excluded from the US-listed candidate universe unless held through public parents or partners.

Falsification plan: downgrade this node if enterprise customers adopt model-native agents that bypass incumbent systems of record, if AI features cannibalize SaaS seats faster than they create consumption/work-unit revenue, or if governance/security failures slow autonomous workflow deployment.

node: Enterprise AI automation, agents, and data workflow platforms
summary: Expanded US-listed/US-traded universe for the enterprise AI automation and data workflow platform node. The highest-relevance group is system-of-record and workflow-control software vendors with embedded enterprise data, governance, security, and monetizable agent execution: ServiceNow, Salesforce, Palantir, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, Workday, Adobe, UiPath, IBM, Atlassian. A second group supplies data, observability, security, and real-time context layers needed to make agents useful and governable in production: Snowflake, MongoDB, Datadog, CrowdStrike. Confluent was not included as an independent ticker because current evidence indicates it was acquired by IBM in 2026; IBM is included instead. This is research-universe expansion only, not a trading recommendation.
